title: K-injectivity after tensoring by a principal two-term free complex
statement: Let Y be a scheme in universe t, R a sheaf of commutative rings of universe max(u,t+1) on its small pro-etale site, a a global section of its unit module, I a K-injective unbounded cochain complex of R-module sheaves, and n a natural number. Using the total tensor and module category of [def-sf-integral-hom-reduction-models] and principalKoszul of [def-pur-principal-koszul-quotient-towers], the complex I tensor [R --a^(n+1)--> R] is K-injective. There is no regularity assumption on a.

source.place: paragraph 1: the two-term finite-free quotient resolution; its functorial maps between quotient levels

proof.text: The generic mapBifunctorMappingCone₂Iso identifies tensor with the Koszul cone with the cone of the induced tensor endomorphism of I tensor R[0]. HomologicalComplex.rightUnitor identifies I tensor R[0] with I, so both ends of this cone map are K-injective.

Use CochainComplex.isKInjective_iff_rightOrthogonal. The right orthogonal to the acyclic homotopy subcategory is triangulated. Apply ext_of_isTriangulatedClosed₃ to mappingCone_triangleh_distinguished, and transport K-injectivity back along the tensor-cone isomorphism. This is a complete Lean proof using Mathlib; zero a and arbitrary unbounded I are included.

lean.statement:
theorem isKInjective_tensor_principalKoszul
    (Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{t})
    (R : Sheaf (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt.topology Y) CommRingCat.{max u (t + 1)})
    (a : (SheafOfModules.unit
      ((sheafCompose (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt.topology Y)
        (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u (t + 1)} RingCat.{max u (t + 1)})).obj R)).sections)
    (I : CochainComplex (Modules.{t, u} Y R) ℤ) [I.IsKInjective] (n : ℕ) :
    (((totalTensor.{t, u} Y R).obj I).obj (principalKoszul R a n)).IsKInjective
